lines.text: Paying on time is 35% of a FICO Score. How much squirrel owes is 30%.
lines.say: Paying on time is thirty-five percent of the score. How much squirrel owes is thirty percent.

lines.text: The rest: length of credit history 15%, new credit 10%, credit mix 10%.
lines.say: The rest: account age at fifteen percent, new credit at ten, credit mix at ten.

lines.text: Example: a $600 balance on a $2,000 limit = 30% of available credit in use.
lines.say: Amounts owed tracks credit in use. Six hundred dollars on a two thousand dollar limit is thirty percent.

lines.text: Income, savings and job are not in a FICO Score. The giant acorn stash doesn't count.
lines.say: Income, savings, and your job aren't in it. Squirrel's giant acorn stash doesn't count.

post.title: Your income counts 0% in your FICO Score
post.ig:
Your income counts for 0% of a FICO Score.

FICO weights: payment history 35%, amounts owed 30%, length of history 15%, new credit 10%, credit mix 10%. Scores run 300 to 850.
Example: a $600 balance on a $2,000 limit = 30% of available credit in use.
Income, savings and employment are not in the score.
The average US FICO Score was 695 in April 2015, peaked at 718 in 2023 and was 714 in FICO's August 2026 report.

Sources: myFICO; FICO Credit Insights reports (2025-2026); Experian.
News and education, not financial advice.
